item.title: New Zealand Business Confidence Recovered as Iran War Subsided
item.description: New Zealand business confidence recovered in the second quarter as a tentative US-Iran peace deal helped push down fuel prices, a survey showed.

item.title: Gold Miners Cadillac, Amapa Minerals Add to Canada IPO Rebound
item.description: Cadillac Mines Corp. and Amapa Minerals Holdings Inc. filed for initial public offerings, in the latest sign that the pace of Canadian listings is starting to pick up.

item.title: Oil Holds Gains as Iran Stokes Inflation Worries: Markets Wrap
item.description: Oil held gains and Asian stocks were set to track Wall Street lower after the standoff between the US and Iran intensified, raising concerns that disruptions to energy supplies could accelerate inflation.

item.title: Oil Holds Gains After Trump Reinstates Blockade on Iranian Ships
item.description: Oil steadied after its biggest advance since April, as US President Donald Trump reimposed a blockade on Iranian ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz and demanded payment for all other cargo moving through the waterway.

item.title: After Biden Denied Alabama Coal Waste Bid, Trump Reverses Course
item.description: The Environmental Protection Agency on Monday proposed to approve Alabama’s application to take over issuing certain coal waste permits from the agency, part of a trend under President Donald Trump to transfer more authority from the federal government to states.

item.title: Russian Billionaire Wins Fight to Boot Manager of Biotech Fund
item.description: Russian billionaire Dmitry Rybolovlev’s family trust prevailed in its effort to remove the manager of a bankrupt $2.5 billion venture capital fund it backed.

item.title: 【今朝の5本】仕事を始める前に読んでおきたい厳選ニュース
item.description: ホルムズ通航に20％の対価要求、近く利上げ必要に、ウォール街決算、独VWが5万人削減、円に弱気

item.title: Argentina IPO Pipeline Grows as YPF Power Unit Files For US Listing
item.description: The power-generation unit of Argentina’s state-run energy firm YPF SA has filed for a US initial public offering, joining a growing pipeline of Argentine companies seeking New York listings.

item.title: Afore Banamex Chief Investment Officer Acosta to Leave Firm
item.description: The chief investment officer of Mexican pension fund Afore Banamex, Tomas Acosta, is leaving the firm, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Fed Maintains Reserve Management Purchases at $10 Billion
item.description: The Federal Reserve said Monday it will buy about $10 billion of Treasury bills this period, unchanged from the previous two cycles, as policymakers seek to bolster reserves in anticipation of a drain in the coming months.

item.title: Lonsdale Suggests Forgoing Patents to Avoid China Taking IP
item.description: China is actively appropriating intellectual property developed by US-based artificial intelligence and life-science startups, 8VC founder Joe Lonsdale told Bloomberg TV Monday.

item.title: NJ Takes Step Toward New Nuclear Plants as Sherrill Signs Bill
item.description: New Jersey is initiating a process to develop new nuclear power plants to meet rising demand for electricity.

item.title: Canadian Oil Sands Firms Reach Carbon Capture Deal With Alberta
item.description: A group of Canadian oil sands producers reached an agreement with the Alberta and federal governments on next steps toward building a carbon capture and storage system.

item.title: Warsh’s Balance-Sheet Panel Runs Into Market Reality Check
item.description: Wall Street strategists expect a group of senior academics and former policymakers assembled by Chairman Kevin Warsh to review the Federal Reserve’s $6.7 trillion balance sheet will face a difficult balancing act: shrinking the central bank’s holdings without destabilizing funding markets.

item.title: RBC Expands Credit Derivatives Trading as AI Debt Fuels Hedging
item.description: Royal Bank of Canada is expanding its credit derivatives trading business in the US and Europe, betting that multibillion-dollar fundraising for artificial intelligence will fuel demand for hedging products.

item.title: Venezuela’s Inflation Spike Compounds Earthquake Misery
item.description: Venezuela’s monthly inflation more than doubled in June, deepening the hardship for families already reeling from the devastation caused by the twin earthquakes of June 24.

item.title: Goldman Pitches Investors on Loans to Their Own Private Funds
item.description: For years, Goldman Sachs Group Inc. has provided key financing to private markets funds that bridges the gap between when they receive investor commitments and when they actually deploy that money.

item.title: Calpers Notches 14.8% Return in Fiscal 2026, Driven By Stocks
item.description: The California Public Employees’ Retirement System reported a 14.8% gain for its latest fiscal year, with results driven by stocks and private equity.

item.title: Waller Says Fed May Need to Raise Rates to Tame Core Inflation
item.description: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said policymakers may need to raise rates in the near term if underlying inflation continues to signal broad price pressures.

item.title: Iran Shipped 57 Million Barrels of Crude Between US Blockades
item.description: Iran managed to export at least 57 million barrels of crude during a brief gap between two American naval blockades, highlighting what’s at stake for the global oil market now that restrictions are being reimposed.

item.title: First Public Fusion Company Surges in Wall Street Trading Debut
item.description: General Fusion Group Ltd. surged in its first day of trading after merging with a blank-check firm, a sign of investors’ interest in the world’s first publicly listed nuclear fusion company.

item.title: Financing the AI Buildout is About to Get Trickier
item.description: Hyperscalers will need to get more creative.

item.title: Russia’s Oil Output Falls to Lowest in at Least 2 1/2 Years
item.description: Russia’s crude output declined to the lowest in at least two and a half years in June as Ukraine attacked the nation’s oil infrastructure on an almost daily basis.

item.title: Europe Risks ‘Explosive’ Path If It Doesn’t Fix Debts, IMF Warns
item.description: Europe’s sovereign-debt dynamics are in danger of going badly awry if the region doesn’t get a grip on its public finances, the International Monetary Fund said.

item.title: More Than 200 Experts Urge Action to Steer AI for Society’s Good
item.description: A group of top economists and artificial intelligence researchers called for more study of the technology’s likely impact, saying it may become “radically more powerful” over the next decade and needs to be steered in a human-friendly direction.

item.title: Connecticut Towns Face Water-Fee Hikes as Bonds Finance Buyout
item.description: Dozens of towns in the state known for its hedge funds and Wall Street commuters are about to feel the impact of a rare type of leveraged buyout.

item.title: FCC Cutting Satellite Approval Lag In Half, Chairman Says
item.description: The Federal Communications Commission has reduced by half the backlog of satellite application approvals as it broadly seeks to stimulate the space and communications economy, Chairman Brendan Carr said in an interview on Bloomberg TV.

item.title: Zurich Ranks Top in Disposable Income Poll Despite $7 Coffees
item.description: Zurich and Geneva may be the most expensive places in the world to buy your meat and veg but it’ll still pay off as the two Swiss cities top a new survey of the highest disposable incomes in the world.

item.title: Apollo’s Slok Warns of Dollar’s Vulnerability to an AI Pullback
item.description: The dollar’s recent gains are at risk if the selloff in artificial intelligence stocks deepens, according to Apollo Global Management Inc.’s Torsten Slok.

item.title: Sunrun Offers Solar Users Hundreds Per Month in Compute Program
item.description: Sunrun Inc. is piloting a program aimed at enabling customers to earn hundreds of dollars per month that would use electricity from rooftop solar installations to power distributed computing, according to Chief Executive Officer Mary Powell.
